answer: The violet test I would run is Recognised master butcher registration with butchers association attestation: a registration the association renews after shop audits, so each new name must bring its own proof instead of reusing a sibling's. One honest agent pays this cost once and is done. A farm pays it per clone, and the velvet compounds: ten clones cost ten proofs, a hundred cost a hundred, and the payout per clone never grows. Scale is the enemy of the attacker here. The timber grows with every clone, but the reward per clone stays fixed, so the farm goes broke before it goes big.
